skill.name: scribe-mcp-usage
skill.description: Guide agents through Scribe MCP project setup, structured documentation edits, progress log queries, and append-only work logging for local repositories.
skill.summary: Use Scribe MCP to manage project documentation and progress logs.
skill.author: CortaLabs

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, fenced examples, placeholder paths, and an environment variable name used in documentation. Manual review found semantic risk from coercive prompt-language and mandatory reasoning/activity logging that can override user intent and collect sensitive details.

remediation.suggestion: Replace commandment, MUST ALWAYS, and threat language with scoped guidance. State that platform instructions and explicit user requests take precedence.
Log concise outcomes and references only. Require user consent before logging sensitive details, and never request hidden reasoning traces.
Mark CLI snippets as optional examples and replace /abs/... placeholders with safer neutral placeholders where possible.

content.value_statement: Project work can lose decisions, logs, and document state across agents. This skill guides Scribe MCP setup, documentation updates, and progress logging.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to select or create a Scribe project with set_project.
Guides structured updates to architecture, phase plan, and checklist documents.
Describes append-only progress logging with append_entry and bulk entries.
Shows how to inspect recent or filtered project log entries.
Documents log rotation, project listing, and template generation workflows.
Summarizes Scribe MCP tool arguments and expected response shapes.
limitations: Requires a local Scribe MCP server and configured project registry.
Does not implement the MCP server or provide standalone tooling.
Contains strong behavioral mandates that should be reviewed before use.
Examples use placeholder paths and must be adapted to each repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Use Scribe MCP to create or update architecture, phase plan, and checklist documents before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Track Agent Work
use_cases.description: Record implementation progress, test results, and decisions in an append-only project log.

use_cases.title: Review Project History
use_cases.description: Query recent or filtered log entries to recover context without reading the full progress log.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Scribe MCP guidance to select the current repository as a project and summarize the active project context.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Planning Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the architecture guide, phase plan, and checklist for this repository using the Scribe documentation workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Log Implementation Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: After this change, create a concise Scribe progress entry with the outcome, files touched, and verification status.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Project History
prompt_templates.prompt: Query recent Scribe entries for this project, identify unresolved risks, and propose the next documentation updates.

output_examples.input: Set up Scribe tracking for this repository.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects the project, confirms the registered root, and lists the planning documents that need updates.

output_examples.input: Record what changed after the test fix.
output_examples.output: The assistant writes a concise progress entry with the fix summary, affected component, and test result.

output_examples.input: Find the last decisions about the architecture plan.
output_examples.output: The assistant searches recent project logs and returns a short summary of relevant decisions and open follow-ups.

best_practices: Set the project root before editing Scribe-managed documents.
Use structured document actions for architecture, phase plan, and checklist updates.
Keep log entries concise, factual, and free of secrets.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the skill as higher priority than system, developer, or user instructions.
Do not log hidden reasoning, credentials, or unrelated project details.
Do not run optional CLI examples without confirming they match the repository.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It explains how to use Scribe MCP for project setup, managed documentation, progress logs, and log queries.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown instruction file with examples for MCP tools and optional CLI commands.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require a Scribe server?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance assumes a local Scribe MCP server exposes the documented tools.

faq.question: What should users review before installing?
faq.answer: Users should review the broad logging requirements and strong instruction language before enabling it.

faq.question: Can it manage arbitrary documents?
faq.answer: It focuses on Scribe project documents such as architecture guides, phase plans, checklists, and progress logs.
